subject: Mobile Development
title: Public Wi-Fi Dangers
description: A 60-second lesson on Public Wi-Fi Dangers.

hook.text: You connect to free Wi-Fi at a coffee shop. Someone is watching every request you send.

buildup.text: Man-in-the-middle attacks intercept traffic on unsecured networks between you and the server.

discovery.text: Attackers can create fake Wi-Fi networks with names like 'Starbucks Free' to lure victims.

twist.text: HTTPS has made most traffic encrypted, but DNS queries and metadata can still be captured.

climax.text: Public Wi-Fi is less dangerous than it was, but caution with sensitive data remains essential.

punchline.text: Free Wi-Fi can cost you your privacy.

quiz.question: What is a man-in-the-middle attack?
options: Intercepting traffic between your device and the server
